output.brief: The rejections trace to a data error in the new booking system, not to the fungicide, the carrier or Lower Serra growers. The mandarin product record in Tallis was copied from avocados and kept a 7.0°C carriage temperature. Our specification is 4.0°C. Every Meridane container booked through Tallis (K3, K4, K6, K8, K9) was sent at 7.0°C, ran at that temperature, and was rejected with 9–14% decay. Every container booked at 4.0°C passed, including K5 and K7 on the new fungicide, and K1 on Meridane's route. So Pellacor and the transshipment route are not the cause, and Meridane ran to the setpoint we gave it. Lower Serra fruit did worse inside rejected containers, but it was 28–40% of each one. It may be a secondary effect, and it doesn't explain the rejections. I'm quite confident. Next steps: correct PRD-MAND-01 to 4.0°C today. Have Meridane reset the container at sea (sailed 3 Oct) and the one queued for 10 Oct. Add a check of reefer settings against the product spec before submission. Review the product-master sign-off. Hold the cargo claim, the Lower Serra suspension and the fungicide reversal. Loggers in containers are reasonable as a short-term safeguard.
